appraisal_events.evidence: « Rachel avait aposté dans la salle un certain nombre d'amis et d'amies dont le rôle était de décontenancer par leurs sarcasmes la débutante, qu'on savait timide, de lui faire perdre la tête de façon qu'elle fît un fiasco complet » ; le narrateur parle ensuite de « la méchanceté » et des « bourreaux de cette débutante ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator holds Rachel responsible for a premeditated act of cruelty that destroys a timid debutante's début, and his framing (his pain at 'la méchanceté', the word 'bourreaux', his shame at not having stopped it) plainly condemns her rather than merely reporting the scene.

appraisal_events.evidence: « la nature de l'illusion dont Saint-Loup était victime à l'égard de Rachel » ; de près elle n'est qu'« une nébuleuse, une voie lactée de taches de rousseur, de tout petits boutons, rien d'autre » ; il était « tout prêt à donner sa fortune et son nom » pour elle, et « elle n'adressa même pas cette fois-là la parole à Saint-Loup ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator dissects Saint-Loup's love as an optical illusion produced by theatrical distance, exposing him as the dupe of his own dream, ready to stake his fortune and name on a bit-player who does not even speak to him.

status_effects.explanation: Rachel is clearly lowered as the organizer of a cruel, premeditated hazing that the narrator finds too painful to speak of and whose perpetrators he calls executioners.

Her standing is deflated by the demystifying account: she plays 'un rôle presque de simple figurante', and was, days before Saint-Loup's love, only 'une apparition fortuite, inconnue, indifférente' on the boards.

Saint-Loup loses local leverage: he is governed by Rachel 'comme ces astres qui nous gouvernent par leur attraction', ready to surrender fortune and name, and is passed over without a word at their first meeting.

ambiguities: The narrator's meditation on cruelty partly extenuates Rachel — he denies the wicked any 'pure et voluptueuse cruauté' and grants that she believed she was avenging good taste and punishing 'une mauvaise camarade' — so the blame is complicated by an understanding of her motives without being withdrawn; a softer reading (-1) is defensible.

The distance passage cuts both ways for Rachel: seen close up she dissolves into freckles and pimples, but at the right distance her nose is 'si fin, si pur' that one would wish to possess her. The demystification is aimed primarily at the mechanism of Saint-Loup's desire, so it is underdetermined whether Rachel herself is diminished or merely relativized.
